speaker: Doctor
text: Since you haven't provided the patient's initial complaint yet, please describe the painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg in detail, including how long it has been present and any associated symptoms like fever or chills.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and steroid use puts you at higher risk for severe infections or atypical reactions. Did the lesion develop rapidly after the ant bite, and have you noticed any red streaks spreading from the site, increased warmth, or pus drainage? Also, have you experienced any fever, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma Gangrenosum secondary to Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection.

The combination of a painful, necrotic ulcer with purplish borders at an ant bite site in a patient with diabetes, immunosuppression from steroid use, and venous insufficiency is highly suggestive of Pseudomonas ecthyma gangrenosum. I need to confirm the presence of systemic signs of sepsis and visualize the extent of tissue involvement.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Differential, Blood Cultures, and Blood Glucose.
REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Skin_Lesion_Right_Leg.
